subject: DPA: private deployment, customer-managed keys & subprocessor boundaries
messages:
From: Dwight Schrute <dwight@acme.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Corp Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: DPA and key management for private deployment

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. We're evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for a pilot and Legal asked for clarification on a couple of points before we proceed: 

1) Can Acme provision and retain sole control of encryption keys (customer-managed keys) when Redwood software is deployed in our VPC/on-prem? 
2) Assuming keys are customer-controlled, will Redwood ever be able to decrypt customer data (logs, request payloads, cached KV) for debugging or support? If so, under what conditions and with what audit trail?
3) Please list the subprocessors involved in Private deployments (if any) and clarify whether any subprocessors will have access to customer-managed keys or plaintext.
4) Cross-border data transfers: Acme processes EU personal data; confirm whether Redwood will transfer any telemetry/usage data outside the EU, and if so, what safeguards are in place (SCCs, binding rules, etc.).

Can you send us the exact DPA language (or addendum) that covers customer-controlled keys and subprocessors? Legal would like draft language to share with their InfoSec and Procurement teams.

Appreciate it — we have an internal deadline next week.

Best,
Dwight
Head of Infrastructure
Acme Corp

---
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Dwight Schrute <dwight@acme.com>
Cc: Acme Corp Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA and key management for private deployment

Hi Dwight —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front:

- Yes: for VPC and on-prem Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (bring your own key / external KMS) so Redwood services never ingest plaintext keys.
- No (by default): Redwood does not have the cryptographic material required to decrypt customer-protected data when keys are customer-managed.
- Subprocessors: for Private deployments we minimize subprocessors; in many on-prem cases there are none. For VPC deployments in cloud regions we may use a small set of cloud infra subprocessors (listed below) but they do not receive keys or plaintext.
- Data transfers: Redwood collects limited telemetry (metrics, anonymized error traces) from Private control-plane interactions; for EU customers we support SCCs and can set hosting regions to the EU.

I'm attaching a short addendum with proposed DPA language that covers key boundaries, subprocessors, and transfer safeguards (filename: Redwood_DPA_Keystore_Addendum_v1.pdf). That should be a good starting point for Legal.

Couple of clarifying notes that your team may care about:
- Operational support: we offer an opt-in support workflow where customers can explicitly create a time-limited support bundle. If you choose that route we never decrypt customer data ourselves — we provide structured telemetry and logs that are filtered and redacted unless you authorize deeper access. Any escalation that requires additional access would go through a documented approval path and is logged.
- Debugging on on-prem installs: our ops engineers can run nondestructive diagnostics in your environment (agent or runbooks) without exfiltrating encrypted blobs.

If Legal wants language changes, loop in Rishi (cc'd) from our legal/partnerships side and Vivek for infra specifics.

Thanks — will follow up with Rishi and Vivek internally.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Keystore_Addendum_v1.pdf (12 KB, PDF)

Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: DPA and key management for private deployment — Acme follow-up

Team — forwarding Acme's email and my reply. Need quick confirmation on a couple items before I send them a near-final addendum: 

1) Can we confirm the exact subprocessors for a VPC deployment in aws-us-east-1? I believe it's: AWS (infrastructure), Datadog (optional telemetry), and Fastly for edge routing in some regions. None should have access to plaintext or keys.

2) For customer-managed KMS: our recommended pattern is customer provides a KMS endpoint (AWS KMS or on-prem HSM) that signs/decrypts locally in their network; Redwood control-plane stores only a reference (key-id) and never stores key material. Can Vivek confirm we have no fallback path where Redwood could obtain key material?

3) Support workflow: Legal asked what the audit trail looks like if a customer authorizes deeper troubleshooting. We should state that any support access is scoped, time-limited, requires named approvals, and is logged to both customer and Redwood audit logs. Monica — can you draft the wording (2–3 sentences) we can paste into the addendum describing approvals and logging?

Please reply by EOD Monday — Acme wants this for procurement review next week.

Thanks,
Neha

Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA and key management for private deployment

Hi Dwight / Acme Legal —

Thanks for the patience. Per our internal review (see cc'd):

- Subprocessors (VPC, aws-us-east-1): AWS (EC2, EBS, S3) and optionally Datadog for metrics. Fastly is not used in the US VPC pattern unless edge caching is turned on. None of these subprocessors receive customer-managed keys or plaintext.

- Customer-managed keys: our model is BYOK with an external KMS/HSM endpoint in your network or cloud account. Redwood stores only key references (key IDs) in our control-plane; we do not store key material. There is no standard fallback that provides Redwood with key material. Any exceptional path to obtain access would require a documented, auditable process with explicit customer authorization.

- Support & audit: we will include the following blurb in the DPA addendum (language below) — feel free to suggest edits.

Proposed addendum paragraph (for your procurement team):
"For Private deployments where Customer elects to use customer-managed keys (\"CMK\"), Redwood shall not have access to the cryptographic key material used to protect Customer Data. Redwood will store only a non-secret reference to the CMK. In the event Customer authorizes Redwood to perform elevated troubleshooting that requires temporary access to decrypted data, such access shall be strictly time-limited, subject to named approvals from authorized Customer representatives, and recorded in both Customer and Redwood audit logs with the scope and justification captured."

- Data transfers: telemetry from the control-plane can be restricted to the EU region for EU customers. We are prepared to execute SCCs and include the standard clauses in the DPA addendum.

Next steps: I attached the addendum (Redwood_DPA_Keystore_Addendum_v1.pdf) which includes the paragraph above and a subprocessors list. If this looks good, Legal can redline and we can route to DocuSign.

If you want a quick call to walk through wording, I can set up 30 minutes with Rishi and Vivek this week.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Keystore_Addendum_v1.pdf (12 KB, PDF)
